newsitem.title: FRANCE: France ready to meet some of truckers' demands.
newsitem.headline: France ready to meet some of truckers' demands.

text.p: The French government said on Tuesday it was ready to help meet some of the key demands of striking French truck drivers by facilitating early retirement and reducing payroll taxes.

Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told Radio Luxembourg: "The state is ready to take responsibility, in particular by facilitating an agreement on cessation of activities and by contributing to reducing social charges."

He was speaking after talks between employers and drivers demanding higher pay, shorter working hours and earlier retirement broke off without an agreement after an all-night session. They are due to resume at 1400 GMT.
Lamassoure said substantial progress had been made in the talks, chaired by a government mediator and he hoped for a rapid conclusion.

The drivers, who have blockaded provincial highways and fuel depots for the last nine days, are demanding a 10 percent wage rise, payment for all hours worked and the right to retire at 55. Employers are seeking a cut in payroll taxes to help finance the drivers' demands.
Lamassoure, who is also budget minister, said the state could also play a role by checking that employers respected a 1994 agreement on pay and conditions which drivers accuse them of flouting.

"I think everyone is well aware that there is no interest in extending the dispute to other sctors. It certainly isn't in the interest of road haulage employees, because some of their demands are legitimate," he said.
"We are working in the negotiations to improve their situation. Diluting the issue would not not be to their benefit," he added.
